title: Schema-first TypeScript emitter: lightweight discriminator maps + Zod/JSON-Schema runtime adapters
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: produce a compact, ergonomic TypeScript client codegen that emits type-safe discriminated unions and lightweight runtime helpers for validating structured output across both batch and streaming LLM responses. This ticket covers a schema-first flow (OpenAPI/JSON-Schema-like input) that generates: 1) strongly typed TypeScript union types, 2) Zod validators for runtime checks, 3) a minimal discriminator map used during streaming incremental parse to route partial chunks to the correct parser, and 4) an optional JSON-Schema drop-in for external tooling. Primary constraints: keep bundle size low for browser/edge usage, avoid large runtime dependencies for serverless customers, and ensure streaming ergonomics (progressive parsing and partial-object recovery) for low-latency consumer features.
acceptance_criteria: Codegen emits a TypeScript union type for each schema with a canonical 'type' discriminator field (configurable).
Zod validators generated alongside types with an API: validate(obj) => {success, errors} and parseIncremental(chunk) helper for streaming partials.
Streaming discriminator map is included as a tiny runtime (<= 1.8 KB gzipped) that can dispatch on partial tokens and guide progressive parse.
Bundled outputs available for node (cjs/esm) and browser (esm) with tree-shakeable exports.
End-to-end example: codegen + zod validator used to parse a streaming chat response that emits two different union variants mid-stream without full reparse.
design_decisions: Prefer codegen-first: generate Zod schemas at build time instead of shipping a large reflective runtime, reduces bundle size and improves error messages.
Discriminator strategy: default to explicit 'type' field but allow user-configurable path (e.g., header.tag, metadata.kind) to support legacy model outputs.
Streaming parsing: use a small state machine that accumulates token-level buffers and applies discriminator heuristics early; fallback to full-parse on ambiguity to maintain correctness.

Tradeoffs: runtime-less codegen reduces dev ergonomics for quick prototypes but is aligned with our performance & bundle-size goals; we provide a single optional runtime package for dev-mode convenience.
tasks: Design doc: finalize schema convention and discriminator config options (Confluence link in attachments).
Codegen: implement emitter module that takes JSON-schema-like input and emits .d.ts + .ts Zod schemas.
Runtime: implement streaming-dispatch helper (small state machine) with adapters for Zod incremental parsing.
Examples: add two end-to-end examples in the monorepo - chat-streaming multi-variant example and embed-generation structured response example.
Tests: unit tests for generated validators, fuzz tests for partial-chunk streaming parse, and e2e integration test against hosted API toy model.
Docs: update SDK docs with migration guide and best-practices for discriminator design.
